key_facts: 78-year-old man presented with painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis
Previous medical history included elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy
Previous treatments with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin showed no improvement
Routine blood test results were within normal limits
Cultures, assays, and blood tests evaluating for viral, bacterial, or fungal etiology were negative
Biopsy of the glans penis ulcer showed dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes
PCR analysis revealed a clonal IgH gene rearrangement
PET-CT scan demonstrated FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic lymph nodes

raw.rationale: The presence of a dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes that are CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+, along with a clonal IgH gene rearrangement, is most consistent with a diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, which is a common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that can present with extranodal involvement, including skin lesions.

rejected.label: Mantle cell lymphoma
rejected.why: Mantle cell lymphoma typically presents with a more indolent course and is less likely to cause a rapidly progressive ulcerative lesion.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous follicle center lymphoma
rejected.why: This type of lymphoma typically presents with more localized skin lesions and lacks the aggressive features seen in this case.

rejected.label: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This type of lymphoma typically presents with nasal or upper respiratory tract involvement and is less likely to cause a penile lesion.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The lymphocytes in this case are B-cell type (CD20+, CD79a+, CD5+), which is not consistent with a T-cell lymphoma.
